post.description:
Exchange a signed one-time assertion for a short-lived token for the agent's principal. Nothing is read from a header the caller sets:
the company and client come from the assertion only to choose where to look, and the token is minted only if the signature verifies against
the PUBLIC keys stored with the approved build. The token is bound to the signing key (DPoP) and carries the gateway scope, so every later
call is still governed (authority, mandate, policy, the tool cap).

Response Register Api Client V1 Machine Api Clients Post

post.description:
Record a runtime attestation signed by an attestor this cell trusts (MACHINE-001 §9, §21). The signature is the
only credential: the tenant is read from the signed SPIFFE ID, the claims are checked only after the signature
passes, and an out-of-date but genuinely signed statement is kept as a FAILED record so the refusal is evidence.

post.description:
The digest an image name points at today, asked of its registry (CR-065). Changes nothing: a person registers what it returns, and a second
person approves it. The registry is contacted outside the database transaction, only if it is one the operator named.

schema.title: Response Resolve Build V1 Machine Builds Resolve Post

post.description:
The versions (tags) an image repository has, so a person picks one instead of typing it. Changes nothing, and the same rules as `:resolve`:
named registries only, public images only. A picked tag is still turned into a digest by `:resolve` before anything is registered.

post.description: Would this call be allowed right now? The real gateway runs and its transaction is thrown away, so nothing is granted, recorded, reserved or metered. ALLOW, DENY, APPROVAL_REQUIRED or UNAVAILABLE, with the reasons.

schema.title: Response Preflight Tool Call V1 Machine Tool Calls Preflight Post

post.description:
The caller is the tool's own server: the grant's audience must be the caller's principal id, so a grant that
leaks to another service is worthless there. The chain is checked again now, and the grant is marked used.
